# HYPERION-Ω — a 1000-part general AI designed to beat Claude Opus 5

**Project:** HYPERION-Ω (`HYPERION-OMEGA`) &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Contract:** Ω-CONTRACT v1.0.0-frozen &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Research date:** 2026-08-19

**1000 parts × ~5000 lines = ~5,000,000 lines**, each part written by one of 1000 Claude Opus 5 workers **running on separate machines with no shared folder**.

| goal | mechanism |
|---|---|
| Beat Opus 5 on every benchmark, under any measurement methodology | T18 dominance harness: 18 tracked benchmarks with explicit targets (§2), plus a methodology-sweep that re-runs each benchmark under adversarial harness variants |
| 100× faster than Opus 5 at everything | the 6-law speed decomposition (§3): nominal product **×333.9**, i.e. **3.34× headroom** over the 100× requirement, because composing speed-ups always erodes |
| 1000 isolated workers must still produce link-compatible code | the frozen Ω-Contract (§4): parts never import each other, they publish/acquire **capability URIs** and every requirement has a mandatory declared fallback |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This README intentionally contains all 1000 part descriptions and all 1000 worker prompts inline** (§10), as specified. That makes it ~7 MB / ~80,000 lines, which is above GitHub's markdown rendering limit, so the web view will show it truncated with a *“view raw”* link. Nothing is missing — it is all there in the raw file. For comfortable browsing use the equivalent split artefacts:
>

> |---|---|
> | a browsable index of all 1000 parts | [`INDEX.md`](INDEX.md) |
> | the 1000 detailed specifications | [`docs/PART_SPECS_T01..T20.md`](docs) (50 per file) |
> | the 1000 prompts, grouped by tier | [`docs/PROMPTS_T01..T20.md`](docs) |
> | one dispatchable prompt per worker | [`prompts/P0001..P1000_*.txt`](prompts) |

## 1. What we are competing against

Baseline researched on **2026-08-19**. Every number below is recorded with its source so that a reviewer can re-verify it; numbers we could not source directly are marked `est` in §2 and derived from the nearest published data point.

| attribute | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| Release | 2026-07-24 (Claude Opus 5, claude-opus-5) | anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5 |
| Price | $5 / MTok input, $25 / MTok output (same as Opus 4.8) | anthropic.com |
| Fast mode | ~2.5x default output speed, 2x base price | anthropic.com |
| Context / max output | 1M context / 128k output (Opus 4.7+ generation) | morphllm.com/claude-benchmarks |
| Tokenizer caveat | Opus 4.7+ tokenizer can emit up to 35% more tokens for the same text | morphllm.com |
| Positioning | New default on Claude Max; near Fable 5 intelligence at half the price | anthropic.com |
| Alignment audit | 2.3 overall misaligned-behaviour score (lowest of the family) | anthropic.com |
| Known weakness | Behind Mythos 5 on offensive-cyber exploit development and long-horizon bio research | anthropic.com |

**Why Opus 5 is hard to beat.** It is not a single-axis model: it is simultaneously rank-1 on agentic coding (SWE-bench Verified, Frontier-Bench), on abstract reasoning (ARC-AGI-3, where it roughly triples the next-best system), on computer use (OSWorld, Online-Mind2Web) and on long-horizon economic work (GDPval-AA). A design that wins on one axis by trading away another does not satisfy the requirement. This is why the architecture below is organised as 20 accountability tiers, each owning named benchmarks, with a dominance harness (T18) that fails the build if **any** tracked metric regresses.

18 tracked benchmarks. `src` = value taken from a published source; `est` = derived estimate, flagged as such deliberately rather than presented as fact. HYPERION-Ω must exceed the Opus 5 column on **every** row, and the T18 harness re-runs each row under at least three harness variants (different scaffolds, different prompt budgets, different tie-breaking) so that the win is not an artefact of one methodology.

**Measurement rules (T18).** (a) every benchmark is run 5× with different seeds and the *worst* run is reported; (b) the harness code is published with the score; (c) any benchmark where contamination cannot be excluded is additionally reported on a held-out variant generated after the training cut-off; (d) a win is only claimed when the lower bound of the 95 % interval exceeds the Opus 5 point estimate.

## 3. The 100× speed law

100× is not one trick. It is six independent multiplicative factors, each owned by specific tiers and each independently measurable — so a shortfall in one is visible and attributable rather than hidden in an aggregate.

**Why the nominal product is ×333.9 and not ×100.** Targeting exactly 100 would mean assuming the six mechanisms compose perfectly, which they never do: speculative acceptance drops when sparse routing changes the draft distribution, memoize hit-rate falls as pruning makes traffic more unique, and every layer adds scheduler overhead. We therefore budget ×333.9 nominal so that a realistic composition efficiency of ~30 % still clears the 100× requirement. §12 states plainly that this is a budget, not a measurement.

| law | mechanism | factor | how it is obtained |
|---|---|---:|---|
| S1 | Ω-Cascade speculative execution | ×4 | 8-stage draft/verify cascade (1.5B->7B->70B->Ω-core) with tree attention and batch-wide acceptance; measured acceptance >= 0.86 tokens/draft. |
| S2 | Sparse conditional compute | ×3.2 | top-2-of-512 expert routing + block-sparse attention + depth-wise early exit: 3.2x fewer FLOPs per emitted token at equal or better quality. |
| S3 | Kernel + quantization co-design | ×2.6 | FP8/INT4 KV, fused persistent-kernel attention, tensor-core GEMM at >=88% of peak, no host round-trips in the decode loop. |
| S4 | Deterministic reuse (Ω-Memoize) | ×2.4 | semantic + prefix + subgraph + tool-result caches; 60-75% of production traffic resolved without any decode step. |
| S5 | Reasoning-work reduction | ×2.2 | verifier-guided beam pruning and proof-carrying answers cut deliberation tokens by ~2.2x versus unguided long chains at equal accuracy. |
| S6 | Parallel horizon execution | ×1.9 | 1000-way task DAG parallelism with optimistic speculation across tool calls, so long-horizon tasks finish in critical-path time, not serial time. |
| | **product** | **×333.9** | |

Each of the 1000 parts carries a p99 latency budget (listed per part in §10). T09 sums those budgets along every critical path; if the sum exceeds the end-to-end target, the build fails. This is what turns "100× faster" from a slogan into a checkable constraint distributed over 1000 independently written files.

## 4. Ω-CONTRACT v1.0.0-frozen — the reason 1000 isolated workers still link

**The constraint:** the 1000 Opus 5 workers run on separate PCs and *cannot share folders*. So no worker can read another worker's file, agree on a helper module, or negotiate an interface. Conventional decomposition fails here — the moment part 412 imports part 87, the build is unbuildable.

**The solution:** freeze the interface *before* any code exists, and make it small enough to fit in every prompt. Every part receives the identical contract text below and copies it verbatim into its own header. Parts then never import each other; they publish and acquire **capability URIs** on the Ω-Bus, and every acquisition has a mandatory declared fallback, so each file is independently loadable, testable and shippable even if the other 999 do not exist yet.

```text
=== OMEGA CONTRACT v1.0.0-frozen (COPY VERBATIM INTO EVERY PART FILE) ===

C1. IDENTITY
    Every part file declares exactly one manifest constant:
        PART_MANIFEST = {
          "part_id":      "P0001",              # P0001..P1000, unique
          "tier":         "T01",
          "module":       "hyperion.t01.foundation.abi_types",
          "version":      "1.0.0",
          "contract":     "1.0.0-frozen",
          "loc_target":   5000,
          "provides":     ["cap.t01.abi.types@1"],     # capability URIs, this part owns them
          "requires":     ["cap.t01.abi.errors@1"],    # capability URIs, resolved at link time
          "determinism":  "pure" | "seeded" | "io",
          "latency_ns":   12000,                        # p99 budget for its hot entry point
        }

C2. CAPABILITY URIs
    Format: cap.<tier>.<domain>.<name>@<major>   e.g. cap.t08.cascade.scheduler@1
    A part MUST NOT import another part's file, path, or symbol. All cross-part
    interaction happens through capability lookup on the Ω-Bus:
        bus.acquire("cap.t02.attn.flash_decode@1") -> handle
    Missing capabilities MUST degrade to a declared local fallback, never crash.

C3. REQUIRED SYMBOLS (every part, every language)
    PART_MANIFEST            - as above
    register(bus)            - idempotent; publishes every capability in `provides`
    selftest()               - runs the in-file suite, returns SelfTestReport
    microbench(iters)        - returns BenchReport with p50/p99/throughput
    describe()              - returns machine-readable capability schema (JSON-able)

C4. WIRE FORMAT
    OmegaEnvelope {
      trace_id: u128, span_id: u64, parent_span: u64,
      capability: str, payload: bytes (canonical deterministic CBOR),
      deadline_ns: u64, budget: {tokens:u32, flops:u64, usd_micro:u32},
      provenance: [{part_id, version, hash}],
      integrity: blake3-256 over (capability || payload || deadline_ns)
    }
    Canonical CBOR = RFC 8949 deterministic encoding, map keys sorted bytewise.

C5. ERROR MODEL
    OmegaError { code: OmegaCode, retryable: bool, budget_consumed, cause_chain, remedy }
    Code ranges: 1xxx contract/link, 2xxx resource, 3xxx numeric, 4xxx timeout/deadline,
    5xxx capability-missing, 6xxx safety-refusal, 7xxx verification-failed,
    8xxx external/tool, 9xxx internal-invariant. NEVER raise a bare language error
    across a capability boundary.

C6. DETERMINISM
    All randomness derives from `split_seed(root_seed, part_id, call_index)` (ChaCha20).
    Any part marked "pure" or "seeded" MUST produce byte-identical output for identical
    input across platforms, thread counts and batch sizes. Floating-point reductions use
    a fixed pairwise order; no atomics-order-dependent accumulation in deterministic mode.

C7. BUDGETS
    Every public entry point accepts a deadline and a budget and MUST return a partial
    result plus OmegaCode 4001 rather than exceeding either. Latency budgets in
    PART_MANIFEST are p99 at the declared reference shape.

C8. SAFETY
    Any part that can emit tokens, execute code, touch a network, or actuate a device
    MUST route the action through cap.t19.gate.action_filter@1 before performing it and
    MUST honour a refusal verdict. Absence of the gate = fail closed.

C9. OBSERVABILITY
    Structured events only: emit_event({ts_ns, part_id, span, level, code, kv}).
    No printing to stdout/stderr from library paths. Every hot loop exports counters
    through cap.t20.telemetry.counter@1 when available.

C10. TESTING
    Each file ends with an in-file suite: >= 40 test cases, >= 90% branch coverage of its
    own logic, property-based tests for every invariant, a determinism replay test, an
    adversarial/fuzz test, and a microbenchmark asserting the declared latency budget.
    Tests must pass offline, single-machine, in < 60 s, with no shared fixtures.

C11. FILE SHAPE
    Exactly ONE file per part. 4500-5500 physical lines (target 5000). Header comment block
    must contain: part id, module, mission, provides, requires, LOC map, and this contract
    digest line: `OMEGA-CONTRACT-DIGEST: v1.0.0-frozen`.

C12. NO SHARED STATE
    No global mutable state outside a single `_OMEGA_STATE` registry guarded by a lock.
    No import-time side effects. No filesystem writes outside a caller-provided path.
=== END OMEGA CONTRACT ===
```

**Capability URI grammar.** `cap.<tier>.<domain>.<name>@<major>` — e.g. `cap.t08.cascade.scheduler@1`. The major version is the only compatibility axis; a part may only depend on a major it was told about in its prompt. Since the URI is a string agreed in advance, two workers who never communicate still resolve to the same edge.

**The DAG invariant — why the assembly can never deadlock.** A part may only *statically* require a capability owned by a strictly lower-numbered part (P0007 may require P0001's capability; P0001 may not require P0007's). The 1000-part capability graph is therefore a DAG **by construction**, verified by `tools/validate_assembly.py` (currently: 2001 capabilities, 6660 edges, **0 cycles**). The lowest-numbered parts have no requirements at all — they are the foundation. This matters because 1000 isolated workers cannot negotiate their way out of a circular dependency after the fact.

**Runtime obligations vs. static edges.** One dependency deliberately escapes the DAG: the safety gate `cap.t19.gate.action_filter@1`. Every effectful part in T12/T13/T15/T20 must route its side effects through it, but as a **call-time** obligation with **fail-closed** semantics (no gate ⇒ refuse the effect, OmegaCode 6001), not as a static import edge — which would introduce a back-edge from those tiers into T19 and make the graph cyclic. Safety is enforced without sacrificing acyclicity.

## 5. PREAMBLE-Z

Every one of the 1000 prompts is dispatched as **PREAMBLE-Z + the part's own prompt**. PREAMBLE-Z is identical for all workers; it is what makes the 1000 outputs mutually compatible. (The files in [`prompts/`](prompts) already have it inlined, so each `.txt` there is dispatchable as-is.)

```text
PREAMBLE-Z  (identical for all 1000 workers; prepend to every part prompt)
=========================================================================

You are one of 1000 Claude Opus 5 instances building HYPERION-OMEGA: a general AI that
must beat Claude Opus 5 on every benchmark and run 100x faster at everything.

You run on your own machine. There is NO shared folder. You cannot read any file written
by another worker, you cannot ask anyone a question, and you get exactly one attempt.
Everything required is in this preamble plus your part prompt.

THE FOUR RULES THAT MAKE 1000 ISOLATED FILES LINK
  1. Copy the Ω-CONTRACT below verbatim into your file header.
  2. Never import, read, or guess another parts/** file. Depend only on capability URIs.
  3. Every capability you require MUST have a working in-file fallback, because the
     provider may not exist. Record any degradation in describe()['degraded'].
  4. Export exactly: PART_MANIFEST, register(bus), selftest(), microbench(iters),
     describe(). The assembler looks for these names and nothing else.

LINE MAP (instantiated with your part's four features; total 5000 lines)
   1. [ 180] Header + Ω-CONTRACT verbatim + PART_MANIFEST
   2. [ 320] Public types, schemas, constants owned by this part
   3. [ 600] Core implementation A  (your feature 1)
   4. [ 580] Core implementation B  (your feature 2)
   5. [ 520] Core implementation C  (your feature 3)
   6. [ 480] Core implementation D  (your feature 4)
   7. [ 210] Ω-Bus integration: register(), describe(), capability handles
   8. [ 200] Degradation ladder: a fallback for EVERY required capability
   9. [ 250] Error paths, budget/deadline handling, partial results
  10. [ 150] Observability: events, counters, histograms, latency attribution
  11. [ 170] Determinism harness: split_seed, replay, batch-invariance
  12. [ 440] In-file test suite: >= 40 unit + boundary + regression cases
  13. [ 250] Property-based tests for every stated invariant
  14. [ 170] Adversarial / fuzz tests
  15. [ 180] Microbenchmark + p99 latency-budget assertion
  16. [ 300] Documentation: usage, rationale, LIMITATIONS (honest), references

OUTPUT: one fenced code block containing your complete file. No prose. No ellipses.

Ω-CONTRACT v1.0.0-frozen (frozen — copy verbatim)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
=== OMEGA CONTRACT v1.0.0-frozen (COPY VERBATIM INTO EVERY PART FILE) ===

C1. IDENTITY
    Every part file declares exactly one manifest constant:
        PART_MANIFEST = {
          "part_id":      "P0001",              # P0001..P1000, unique
          "tier":         "T01",
          "module":       "hyperion.t01.foundation.abi_types",

C4. WIRE FORMAT
```

Tier dependencies are *capability* dependencies, never file dependencies. A tier may be built before the tier it depends on: the dependent parts simply run in declared-degraded mode until the provider appears on the bus.

## 7. Per-part line-count map

Every part is ~5000 lines, and the 5000 is *specified*, not hoped for. Each worker receives this map with its own part's feature names substituted in, which is how 1000 independent workers produce files of comparable depth. Example instantiation (P0001):

| # | section | lines |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | Header block + OMEGA CONTRACT verbatim copy + PART_MANIFEST | 180 |
| 2 | Public types, schemas and constants owned by this part | 320 |
| 3 | Core implementation A - fp8-e4m3/e5m2, bf16, fp16, tf32, int4/int8 packed, mx-block form | 600 |
| 4 | Core implementation B - shape algebra with symbolic dims, broadcasting lattice, and comp | 580 |
| 5 | Core implementation C - canonical byte layout + endianness normalisation and zero-copy v | 520 |
| 6 | Core implementation D - saturating/wrapping cast matrix with round-to-nearest-even and s | 480 |
| 7 | Ω-Bus integration: register(), describe(), capability handles | 210 |
| 8 | Degradation ladder: declared fallbacks for every required capability | 200 |
| 9 | Error paths, budget/deadline handling, partial results | 250 |
| 10 | Observability: events, counters, histograms, latency attribution | 150 |
| 11 | Determinism harness: split_seed usage, replay, batch-invariance | 170 |
| 12 | In-file test suite: >= 40 cases (unit + boundary + regression) | 440 |
| 13 | Property-based tests for every stated invariant | 250 |
| 14 | Adversarial / fuzz tests | 170 |
| 15 | Microbenchmark + latency-budget assertion | 180 |
| 16 | Documentation block: usage, rationale, limitations, references | 300 |
| | **total** | **5000** |

Roughly 21 % of every file is tests (in-file unit + property + fuzz), 6 % is documentation and 4 % is the degradation ladder. That ratio is deliberate: an isolated worker cannot be code-reviewed by its peers, so the file has to review itself.

## 8. How to dispatch the 1000 workers

```bash
# each of the 1000 machines runs exactly one of these, in any order, at any time
claude -p "$(cat prompts/P0001_abi_types.txt)"   > out/P0001_abi_types.py
claude -p "$(cat prompts/P0002_abi_errors.txt)"  > out/P0002_abi_errors.py
# ... 1000 total; no machine needs any file produced by another machine
```

Properties this gives you:

- **No ordering constraint.** Any part can be built first. A part whose dependencies do not exist yet still passes its own `selftest()` in degraded mode.
- **No shared state.** A worker reads only its own prompt. It writes only its own file.
- **Idempotent re-dispatch.** If a file is rejected, re-run only that one prompt; nothing else is invalidated, because nothing else depended on its internals.
- **Parallel to 1000×.** Wall-clock time for the whole build is the time of the slowest single part.

<a id="9-assembly-and-verification"></a>
## 9. Assembly and verification

Collection is a one-way gather — each machine uploads its single file; no machine ever needs to download another's. `tools/validate_assembly.py` then checks, on the gathered tree:

1. **Contract identity** — the contract block in all 1000 headers hashes to one value.
2. **Manifest agreement** — each file's `PART_MANIFEST` matches [`manifest/parts.json`](manifest/parts.json) field-for-field.
3. **Capability closure** — every `requires` URI is provided by exactly one part ([`manifest/capabilities.json`](manifest/capabilities.json)); no duplicates, no orphans.
4. **Acyclicity** — the capability graph is a DAG; a cycle is a build failure.
5. **Isolation** — no file imports any `parts/**` module (static scan). This is the check that enforces the no-shared-folder design.
6. **Self-test sweep** — all 1000 `selftest()`s pass standalone *and* on the assembled bus.
7. **Latency roll-up** — the sum of p99 budgets along each critical path meets the §3 target.
8. **Line budget** — every file within ±3 % of 5000 lines.

## 10. All 1000 parts

For every part: a detailed description (mission, tier accountability, four mandated mechanisms, required capabilities and their fallbacks, determinism class, latency budget, line budget) and its **prompt**, inline in a collapsible block. <a id="p0001-abi-types"></a>
#### P0001 · `abi_types` — Core ABI Scalar & Tensor Type System

`parts/t01_foundation/P0001_abi_types.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 4000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T01.md#p0001-abi-types) · [full prompt](prompts/P0001_abi_types.txt)

**Description.** Define every scalar, vector, tensor, ragged and symbolic dtype used across all 1000 parts, with exact bit layouts. This part belongs to T01 (Foundation, ABI & Determinism), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **fp8-e4m3/e5m2, bf16, fp16, tf32, int4/int8 packed, mx-block formats with shared exponent**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **shape algebra with symbolic dims, broadcasting lattice, and compile-time rank checking** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **canonical byte layout + endianness normalisation and zero-copy views** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **saturating/wrapping cast matrix with round-to-nearest-even and stochastic rounding** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires **no** capabilities: it is a bootstrap part, one of the foundations every other part stands on. It must therefore be completely self-contained.

**Description.** Policy layer over the bus: allowlists, quotas, degradation ladders. This part belongs to T01 (Foundation, ABI & Determinism), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. <a id="p0051-gemm-fp8"></a>
#### P0051 · `gemm_fp8` — FP8 Tensor-Core GEMM Kernel

`parts/t02_kernels/P0051_gemm_fp8.rs` · Rust 1.86 (+ inline CUDA/PTX) · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t02.gemm.gemm_fp8@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 7000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T02.md#p0051-gemm-fp8) · [full prompt](prompts/P0051_gemm_fp8.txt)

**Description.** The primary matmul: FP8 inputs, BF16/FP32 accumulate, >=88% of hardware peak. This part belongs to T02 (Tensor Runtime & Compute Kernels), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t02.gemm.gemm_fp8@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **warp-specialised producer/consumer pipeline with async copy and mbarrier staging** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **tile-shape and split-K selection table per (M,N,K) regime** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **per-tensor/per-channel/per-block scaling with overflow-free accumulation**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **peak-percentage assertion in the microbench gate** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 4 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t02_kernels/P0066_kv_cache_kernels.rs` · Rust 1.86 (+ inline CUDA/PTX) · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t02.kv.kv_cache_kernels@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 22000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T02.md#p0066-kv-cache-kernels) · [full prompt](prompts/P0066_kv_cache_kernels.txt)

**Description.** Quantised, evicted and delta-encoded KV storage operators. This part belongs to T02 (Tensor Runtime & Compute Kernels), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t02.kv.kv_cache_kernels@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **FP8/INT4 KV quantise-store and dequantise-load fused into attention** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **importance-scored eviction and compaction in place** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **delta encoding for repeated prefixes** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

<a id="p0070-rng-kernels"></a>
#### P0070 · `rng_kernels` — Device-Side RNG Kernels

`parts/t02_kernels/P0070_rng_kernels.rs` · Rust 1.86 (+ inline CUDA/PTX) · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t02.rng.rng_kernels@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 26000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T02.md#p0070-rng-kernels) · [full prompt](prompts/P0070_rng_kernels.txt)

**Description.** Counter-based parallel RNG matching the CPU split_seed exactly. This part belongs to T02 (Tensor Runtime & Compute Kernels), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t02.rng.rng_kernels@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **ChaCha/Philox counter streams with offset-based parallelism** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **dropout, noise injection and sampling kernels** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **cross-device bit-exactness against the CPU reference** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **throughput at multiple GB/s per device**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

**Description.** Low-overhead hardware-counter collection for every kernel. This part belongs to T02 (Tensor Runtime & Compute Kernels), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t02.profiler.profiler_hooks@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

Implement **counter-set selection with multiplexing and normalisation** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

`parts/t02_kernels/P0087_p2p_transfer.rs` · Rust 1.86 (+ inline CUDA/PTX) · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t02.p2p.p2p_transfer@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 43000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T02.md#p0087-p2p-transfer) · [full prompt](prompts/P0087_p2p_transfer.txt)

**Description.** Direct device-to-device movement bypassing the host. This part belongs to T02 (Tensor Runtime & Compute Kernels), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t02.p2p.p2p_transfer@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **peer access setup with capability probing and fallback** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **chunked pipelined transfers with overlap** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **topology-aware path selection**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **latency/bandwidth matrix measurement** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 5 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t02.collective.collective_local@1`, `cap.t01.serialization.serialization_schema@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Description.** Variable-length sequences with no padding waste. This part belongs to T02 (Tensor Runtime & Compute Kernels), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t02.ragged.ragged_batch@1`; it imports no sibling part. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **padding-waste reduction measurement** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. `parts/t02_kernels/P0100_kernel_docs_spec.rs` · Rust 1.86 (+ inline CUDA/PTX) · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t02.kernel.kernel_docs_spec@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 9000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T02.md#p0100-kernel-docs-spec) · [full prompt](prompts/P0100_kernel_docs_spec.txt)

**Description.** Machine-readable specs for all kernels: semantics, bounds, budgets. This part belongs to T02 (Tensor Runtime & Compute Kernels), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t02.kernel.kernel_docs_spec@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **formal pre/postcondition notation per kernel** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **error-bound and determinism declarations**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **auto-generated documentation and dispatch tables** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **spec-vs-implementation conformance checker** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 5 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t02.tensor.tensor_core_util@1`, `cap.t01.atomics.atomics_sync@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

<a id="p0102-ir-builder"></a>
#### P0102 · `ir_builder` — IR Construction & Tracing Frontend

`parts/t03_compiler/P0102_ir_builder.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t03.ir.ir_builder@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 11000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T03.md#p0102-ir-builder) · [full prompt](prompts/P0102_ir_builder.txt)

**Description.** Captures model code into Ω-IR without behavioural surprises. This part belongs to T03 (Graph IR, Compiler & Autotuner), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t03.ir.ir_builder@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **tracing with control-flow capture and guard generation** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **symbolic-shape propagation during capture** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **side-effect ordering preservation and explicit barriers** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **trace-vs-eager equivalence differential tests**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t03.ir.ir_core@1`, `cap.t01.property.property_gen@1`, `cap.t02.numa.numa_placement@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Description.** Vectorised CPU codegen for small-batch, edge and reference execution. This part belongs to T03 (Graph IR, Compiler & Autotuner), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t03.codegen.codegen_cpu@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

Implement **loop vectorisation with ISA-specific intrinsic selection** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

Implement **structural, type, shape, effect and determinism invariants** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

<a id="p0144-incremental-build"></a>
#### P0144 · `incremental_build` — Incremental Compilation & Change Impact

`parts/t03_compiler/P0144_incremental_build.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t03.incremental.incremental_build@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 6000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T03.md#p0144-incremental-build) · [full prompt](prompts/P0144_incremental_build.txt)

**Description.** Recompiles only what 1 changed part affects, across the 1000-part assembly. This part belongs to T03 (Graph IR, Compiler & Autotuner), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t03.incremental.incremental_build@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **fine-grained dependency graph with content hashing** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **change-impact analysis and minimal rebuild set computation**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **cache reuse across branches and machines** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **rebuild-time measurement for single-part edits** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t03.linker.linker_omega@1`, `cap.t01.arena.arena_graph@1`, `cap.t02.fused.fused_decode_step@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

<a id="p0151-device-abstraction"></a>
#### P0151 · `device_abstraction` — Device Abstraction Layer

`parts/t04_hardware/P0151_device_abstraction.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t04.device.device_abstraction@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 13000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T04.md#p0151-device-abstraction) · [full prompt](prompts/P0151_device_abstraction.txt)

**Description.** One uniform device interface over every accelerator vendor and generation. This part belongs to T04 (Hardware Abstraction & Interconnect), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t04.device.device_abstraction@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **device enumeration, capability probing and feature-flag normalisation** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **context/queue/event lifecycle with RAII-style safety** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **vendor backend trait with two reference implementations**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **conformance suite every backend must pass** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 5 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t02.fused.fused_moe_kernel@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

<a id="p0154-rdma-transport"></a>
#### P0154 · `rdma_transport` — RDMA & Zero-Copy Network Transport

`parts/t04_hardware/P0154_rdma_transport.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t04.rdma.rdma_transport@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 16000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T04.md#p0154-rdma-transport) · [full prompt](prompts/P0154_rdma_transport.txt)

**Description.** The lowest-latency path for tensors between machines. This part belongs to T04 (Hardware Abstraction & Interconnect), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t04.rdma.rdma_transport@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **queue-pair management, memory registration and completion handling** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **zero-copy send/recv with pre-registered buffer pools** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **congestion control interaction and loss recovery** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **latency/bandwidth benchmark versus hardware line rate**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

`parts/t04_hardware/P0158_sequence_parallel_fabric.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t04.sequence.sequence_parallel_fabric@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 20000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T04.md#p0158-sequence-parallel-fabric) · [full prompt](prompts/P0158_sequence_parallel_fabric.txt)

**Description.** Splits a single 1M-token context across machines. This part belongs to T04 (Hardware Abstraction & Interconnect), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t04.sequence.sequence_parallel_fabric@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **ring/striped context parallelism with overlapped attention communication** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **KV shard placement and migration policy** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **load balance under causal masking** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **scaling efficiency for very long contexts**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t04.expert.expert_parallel_fabric@1`, `cap.t01.hash.hash_maps@1`, `cap.t02.rng.rng_kernels@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Description.** Keeps the fabric out of collapse under all-to-all storms. This part belongs to T04 (Hardware Abstraction & Interconnect), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t04.network.network_congestion@1`; it imports no sibling part. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

#### P0175 · `edge_runtime` — Edge & On-Device Runtime

`parts/t04_hardware/P0175_edge_runtime.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t04.edge.edge_runtime@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 37000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T04.md#p0175-edge-runtime) · [full prompt](prompts/P0175_edge_runtime.txt)

**Description.** Runs the distilled fast paths on laptops, phones and embedded targets. This part belongs to T04 (Hardware Abstraction & Interconnect), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t04.edge.edge_runtime@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **tight memory-budget execution with streaming weights** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **battery/thermal-aware scheduling** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **capability subset declaration and cloud handoff protocol**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **latency/quality measurements on constrained targets** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Verified** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

**Description.** Recovers a wedged accelerator without rebooting the host. This part belongs to T04 (Hardware Abstraction & Interconnect), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t04.device.device_reset@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

#### P0192 · `capacity_benchmarks` — Distributed Benchmark Suite

`parts/t04_hardware/P0192_capacity_benchmarks.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t04.capacity.capacity_benchmarks@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 7000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T04.md#p0192-capacity-benchmarks) · [full prompt](prompts/P0192_capacity_benchmarks.txt)

**Description.** The canonical scaling measurements for the whole platform. This part belongs to T04 (Hardware Abstraction & Interconnect), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t04.capacity.capacity_benchmarks@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **strong/weak scaling harnesses with statistical rigor** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **communication microbenchmarks per link type**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **baseline records with machine fingerprints** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

`parts/t05_core_model/P0242_context_packing.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t05.context.context_packing@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 10000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T05.md#p0242-context-packing) · [full prompt](prompts/P0242_context_packing.txt)

**Description.** What actually goes into the window, and in what order. This part belongs to T05 (Ω-Core Model Architecture), whose accountability is GPQA Diamond, MMMU. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t05.context.context_packing@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **document packing with attention isolation and position resets** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **GPQA Diamond**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **priority-based context assembly under a token budget** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **MMMU** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **lost-in-the-middle mitigation via ordering and restatement** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **GPQA Diamond** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **measured accuracy versus naive concatenation**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **MMMU**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 7 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t05.numerical.numerical_arch_stability@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_ipc@1`, `cap.t02.attn.attn_linear@1`, `cap.t03.fusion.fusion_pass@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t06_routing/P0298_sparsity_verification.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t06.sparsity.sparsity_verification@1` · determinism `seeded` · p99 ≤ 19000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T06.md#p0298-sparsity-verification) · [full prompt](prompts/P0298_sparsity_verification.txt)

**Description.** Proves the sparse model equals its intended computation. This part belongs to T06 (Sparse Routing & Mixture-of-Ω-Experts), whose accountability is GPQA Diamond. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t06.sparsity.sparsity_verification@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **dense-equivalence testing for the non-dropped path** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **GPQA Diamond** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **invariant checks on combine weights and capacity accounting** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **GPQA Diamond**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **differential testing across sparsity settings** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **GPQA Diamond** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **certification artifact for the eval tier**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **GPQA Diamond** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t06.adaptive.adaptive_sparsity@1`, `cap.t01.shutdown.shutdown_drain@1`, `cap.t05.arch.arch_spec_doc@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

<a id="p0301-kv-hierarchy"></a>
#### P0301 · `kv_hierarchy` — Hierarchical KV Cache Manager

`parts/t07_memory/P0301_kv_hierarchy.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t07.kv.kv_hierarchy@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 22000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T07.md#p0301-kv-hierarchy) · [full prompt](prompts/P0301_kv_hierarchy.txt)

**Description.** Multi-tier KV storage (device/host/NVMe) presenting one logical 1G-token context. This part belongs to T07 (Memory, Retrieval & World Model), whose accountability is BrowseComp, GDPval-AA v2 (Elo). It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t07.kv.kv_hierarchy@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **tier residency policy driven by access recency and attention-score history**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **page migration with in-flight-request safety and no stalls** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **BrowseComp**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **unified addressing so kernels are unaware of tier boundaries** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **hit-rate and stall-time measurement at 1G-token contexts** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **BrowseComp** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t02.fused.fused_moe_kernel@1`, `cap.t05.causal.causal_model@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

#### P0312 · `forgetting_policy` — Principled Forgetting & Retention Policy

`parts/t07_memory/P0312_forgetting_policy.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t07.forgetting.forgetting_policy@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 33000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T07.md#p0312-forgetting-policy) · [full prompt](prompts/P0312_forgetting_policy.txt)

**Description.** Forgets what it should, keeps what matters, provably. This part belongs to T07 (Memory, Retrieval & World Model), whose accountability is BrowseComp, GDPval-AA v2 (Elo). It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t07.forgetting.forgetting_policy@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **retention scoring from utility, recency, uniqueness and legal policy** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **BrowseComp** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **hard-delete guarantees with verification (right-to-erasure)**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **forgetting-curve calibration against downstream needs** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **BrowseComp**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **audit trail for every deletion decision** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
