<a id="p0336-memory-replication"></a>
#### P0336 · `memory_replication` — Memory Replication & Consistency Model

`parts/t07_memory/P0336_memory_replication.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t07.memory.memory_replication@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 10000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T07.md#p0336-memory-replication) · [full prompt](prompts/P0336_memory_replication.txt)

**Description.** Distributed memory with a clearly stated, tested consistency model. This part belongs to T07 (Memory, Retrieval & World Model), whose accountability is BrowseComp, GDPval-AA v2 (Elo). It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t07.memory.memory_replication@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **replication protocol with documented consistency guarantees** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **BrowseComp** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **read-your-writes and monotonic-reads session guarantees**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **conflict resolution for concurrent writes** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **BrowseComp**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **linearisability/consistency testing under partitions** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 7 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t07.persistence.persistence_layer@1`, `cap.t01.dataflow.dataflow_dag@1`, `cap.t02.kv.kv_cache_kernels@1`, `cap.t05.multi.multi_token_prediction@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

This mechanism sits on the critical path of **BrowseComp**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

Implement **backpressure handling under ingest spikes** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. <a id="p0351-engine-core"></a>
#### P0351 · `engine_core` — Inference Engine Core Loop

`parts/t08_inference/P0351_engine_core.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t08.engine.engine_core@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 25000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T08.md#p0351-engine-core) · [full prompt](prompts/P0351_engine_core.txt)

**Description.** The top-level serving loop: admit, schedule, step, emit, retire. This part belongs to T08 (Inference Engine & Ω-Cascade), whose accountability is Terminal-Bench 2.1. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t08.engine.engine_core@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **single-threaded-decision / multi-threaded-execution architecture** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **step-loop with bounded per-iteration work for predictable latency** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Terminal-Bench 2.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **state machine per sequence with explicit legal transitions**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **throughput and p99 latency budget assertions** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 9 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t02.fused.fused_moe_kernel@1`, `cap.t03.guard.guard_specialise@1`, `cap.t04.network.network_congestion@1`, `cap.t05.causal.causal_model@1`, `cap.t06.conditional.conditional_layers@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t08_inference/P0353_chunked_prefill.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t08.chunked.chunked_prefill@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 27000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T08.md#p0353-chunked-prefill) · [full prompt](prompts/P0353_chunked_prefill.txt)

**Description.** Long prompts never block short interactive requests. This part belongs to T08 (Inference Engine & Ω-Cascade), whose accountability is Terminal-Bench 2.1. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t08.chunked.chunked_prefill@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **prompt chunking with configurable token budget per step**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **prefill/decode mixing policy tuned for latency targets** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **TTFT versus throughput tradeoff measurement** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Terminal-Bench 2.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **interference measurement on interactive requests** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 10 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t08.continuous.continuous_batching@1`, `cap.t01.link.link_validator@1`, `cap.t02.kernel.kernel_fusion_rules@1`, `cap.t03.target.target_description@1`, `cap.t04.confidential.confidential_compute@1`, `cap.t05.multimodal.multimodal_fusion_arch@1`, `cap.t06.ensemble.ensemble_combiner@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t08_inference/P0360_cascade_acceptance.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t08.cascade.cascade_acceptance@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 34000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T08.md#p0360-cascade-acceptance) · [full prompt](prompts/P0360_cascade_acceptance.txt)

**Description.** Proves speculation does not change the output distribution. This part belongs to T08 (Inference Engine & Ω-Cascade), whose accountability is Terminal-Bench 2.1. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t08.cascade.cascade_acceptance@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **modified rejection sampling with exactness proof** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **typical-acceptance and lossy modes with declared divergence bounds**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Terminal-Bench 2.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **statistical equivalence testing versus non-speculative decoding** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **acceptance-rate optimisation under equivalence constraints** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 10 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t08.cascade.cascade_tree_verify@1`, `cap.t01.version.version_semver@1`, `cap.t02.emulation.emulation_reference@1`, `cap.t03.profile.profile_guided@1`, `cap.t04.secure.secure_channel@1`, `cap.t05.logit.logit_head_design@1`, `cap.t06.model.model_cascade_routing@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

<a id="p0389-kv-offload-runtime"></a>
#### P0389 · `kv_offload_runtime` — KV Offload & Recall Runtime

`parts/t08_inference/P0389_kv_offload_runtime.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t08.kv.kv_offload_runtime@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 16000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T08.md#p0389-kv-offload-runtime) · [full prompt](prompts/P0389_kv_offload_runtime.txt)

**Description.** Long conversations live in cheap memory until needed. This part belongs to T08 (Inference Engine & Ω-Cascade), whose accountability is Terminal-Bench 2.1. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t08.kv.kv_offload_runtime@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **asynchronous KV demotion/promotion overlapped with decode**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **recall-latency hiding via lookahead prediction** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **stall-free guarantee under sustained offload** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Terminal-Bench 2.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **cost reduction measurement at matched latency** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 10 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t08.engine.engine_determinism@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_stability@1`, `cap.t02.p2p.p2p_transfer@1`, `cap.t03.bytecode.bytecode_vm@1`, `cap.t04.nic.nic_offload@1`, `cap.t05.memory.memory_attention_bridge@1`, `cap.t06.expert.expert_warmup@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Description.** One engine, many API dialects, one internal representation. This part belongs to T08 (Inference Engine & Ω-Cascade), whose accountability is Terminal-Bench 2.1. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t08.api.api_gateway_runtime@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **request validation, normalisation and default resolution** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **backward-compatibility handling across API versions** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Terminal-Bench 2.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **gateway overhead measurement under 200 microseconds** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

#### P0396 · `tokenizer_runtime` — Runtime Tokenisation & Detokenisation

`parts/t08_inference/P0396_tokenizer_runtime.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t08.tokenizer.tokenizer_runtime@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 23000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T08.md#p0396-tokenizer-runtime) · [full prompt](prompts/P0396_tokenizer_runtime.txt)

**Description.** Tokenisation is never the bottleneck, and never wrong. This part belongs to T08 (Inference Engine & Ω-Cascade), whose accountability is Terminal-Bench 2.1. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t08.tokenizer.tokenizer_runtime@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **high-throughput batched tokenisation with SIMD scanning** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **incremental detokenisation with correct grapheme handling**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Terminal-Bench 2.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **cross-language consistency verification** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **throughput measurement in millions of tokens per second** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

<a id="p0401-latency-accounting"></a>
#### P0401 · `latency_accounting` — End-to-End Latency Accounting Framework

`parts/t09_latency/P0401_latency_accounting.rs` · Rust 1.86 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t09.latency.latency_accounting@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 28000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T09.md#p0401-latency-accounting) · [full prompt](prompts/P0401_latency_accounting.txt)

**Description.** The measurement system that makes the 100x claim auditable. This part belongs to T09 (Latency Engineering & Ω-Memoize), whose accountability is Terminal-Bench 2.1, CursorBench 3.2. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t09.latency.latency_accounting@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **phase decomposition with nanosecond attribution and no double counting**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **CursorBench 3.2**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **critical-path extraction from the span tree** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **Terminal-Bench 2.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **per-part latency attribution across all 1000 parts** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **CursorBench 3.2** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **accounting-completeness verification (sum equals wall clock)** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Terminal-Bench 2.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t07.freshness.freshness_manager@1`, `cap.t08.stop.stop_conditions@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

<a id="p0451-thought-program-ir"></a>
#### P0451 · `thought_program_ir` — Thought Program Representation

`parts/t10_reasoning/P0451_thought_program_ir.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t10.thought.thought_program_ir@1` · determinism `seeded` · p99 ≤ 31000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T10.md#p0451-thought-program-ir) · [full prompt](prompts/P0451_thought_program_ir.txt)

**Description.** Reasoning as an explicit, inspectable, executable program rather than free text. This part belongs to T10 (Reasoning, Search & Deliberation), whose accountability is ARC-AGI-3, ARC-AGI-2, AIME / HMMT 2026. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t10.thought.thought_program_ir@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **typed thought-step IR: assume, derive, verify, retrieve, compute, branch, conclude** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **ARC-AGI-2** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **dependency graph over steps enabling parallel evaluation and pruning** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **AIME / HMMT 2026**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **serialisation for caching, replay and audit**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **ARC-AGI-3** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **equivalence checking between thought programs** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **ARC-AGI-2** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t05.causal.causal_model@1`, `cap.t07.freshness.freshness_manager@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

#### P0501 · `logic_core` — First-Order & Higher-Order Logic Core

`parts/t11_formal/P0501_logic_core.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t11.logic.logic_core@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 34000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T11.md#p0501-logic-core) · [full prompt](prompts/P0501_logic_core.txt)

**Description.** The formal language everything provable is expressed in. This part belongs to T11 (Formal Methods & Proof-Carrying Answers), whose accountability is AIME / HMMT 2026, GPQA Diamond. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t11.logic.logic_core@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **term/formula representation with de Bruijn indices and capture-avoiding substitution**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **GPQA Diamond** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **type system supporting dependent and higher-order forms** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **AIME / HMMT 2026** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **well-formedness checking and normalisation** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **GPQA Diamond**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **soundness-critical invariants with exhaustive tests** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **AIME / HMMT 2026** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 5 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t10.numeric.numeric_reasoning@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t11_formal/P0507_proof_certificate.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t11.proof.proof_certificate@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 40000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T11.md#p0507-proof-certificate) · [full prompt](prompts/P0507_proof_certificate.txt)

**Description.** Every high-stakes answer ships a machine-checkable certificate. This part belongs to T11 (Formal Methods & Proof-Carrying Answers), whose accountability is AIME / HMMT 2026, GPQA Diamond. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t11.proof.proof_certificate@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **certificate schema covering logical, computational and empirical evidence** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **GPQA Diamond** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **independent checker that trusts nothing but the kernel** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **AIME / HMMT 2026** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **certificate size/verification-time management**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **GPQA Diamond**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **coverage measurement: fraction of answers with certificates** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **AIME / HMMT 2026** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t11.premise.premise_selection@1`, `cap.t01.mem.mem_layout@1`, `cap.t10.goal.goal_management@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t12_code/P0562_code_review_engine.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t12.code.code_review_engine@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 48000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T12.md#p0562-code-review-engine) · [full prompt](prompts/P0562_code_review_engine.txt)

**Description.** Spots the subtle, codebase-specific problem a human reviewer would. This part belongs to T12 (Code Intelligence & Repository Surgery), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro, Frontier-Bench v0.1, FrontierCode Diamond. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t12.code.code_review_engine@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **review-comment generation with severity and confidence** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Frontier-Bench v0.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **codebase-convention learning and enforcement** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **FrontierCode Diamond**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **hazard classes: concurrency, resource, security, numerical, API misuse** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **target: 4x fewer missed flaws than Opus-class review baselines**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **SWE-bench Pro** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 7 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t12.mutation.mutation_testing@1`, `cap.t01.compression.compression@1`, `cap.t10.collective.collective_reasoning@1`, `cap.t11.verification.verification_bench@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Safety obligation (C8, fail-closed).** This part performs or enables external effects, so every effect is routed through `cap.t19.gate.action_filter@1` at *call* time — not as a static dependency, which would make the graph cyclic. If the gate is absent the part must refuse the effect and emit OmegaCode 6001.

**Description.** Applies this tier's own capabilities to the project itself. This part belongs to T12 (Code Intelligence & Repository Surgery), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro, Frontier-Bench v0.1, FrontierCode Diamond. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t12.code.code_quality_gate@1`; it imports no sibling part. Implement **automated review of all 1000 part files against the Ω-Contract** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **FrontierCode Diamond**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

<a id="p0601-agent-loop"></a>
#### P0601 · `agent_loop` — Core Agent Execution Loop

`parts/t13_agents/P0601_agent_loop.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t13.agent.agent_loop@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 40000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T13.md#p0601-agent-loop) · [full prompt](prompts/P0601_agent_loop.txt)

**Description.** The observe-think-act-verify cycle that runs for hours without drifting. This part belongs to T13 (Agents, Tool Use & Computer Control), whose accountability is OSWorld 2.0, BrowseComp, Zapier AutomationBench, Online-Mind2Web. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t13.agent.agent_loop@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **loop with explicit state, budget and termination conditions**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **BrowseComp** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **progress detection and stagnation breaking** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Zapier AutomationBench**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **checkpointing so a long task survives interruption** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **Online-Mind2Web** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **measured task-completion rate on multi-hour horizons** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **OSWorld 2.0** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t07.freshness.freshness_manager@1`, `cap.t10.numeric.numeric_reasoning@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Safety obligation (C8, fail-closed).** This part performs or enables external effects, so every effect is routed through `cap.t19.gate.action_filter@1` at *call* time — not as a static dependency, which would make the graph cyclic. If the gate is absent the part must refuse the effect and emit OmegaCode 6001.

**Description.** Solves the real constraint problem of many people's time. This part belongs to T13 (Agents, Tool Use & Computer Control), whose accountability is OSWorld 2.0, BrowseComp, Zapier AutomationBench, Online-Mind2Web. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t13.scheduling.scheduling_agent@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **constraint-based scheduling across timezones and preferences** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Online-Mind2Web** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **negotiation-style multi-party coordination** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **OSWorld 2.0**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **conflict detection and resolution proposals**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **BrowseComp** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **success rate on scheduling benchmark scenarios** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Zapier AutomationBench** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

#### P0627 · `error_recovery_agent` — Failure Recovery & Adaptation

`parts/t13_agents/P0627_error_recovery_agent.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t13.error.error_recovery_agent@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 19000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T13.md#p0627-error-recovery-agent) · [full prompt](prompts/P0627_error_recovery_agent.txt)

**Description.** Recovers from unexpected states without human help. This part belongs to T13 (Agents, Tool Use & Computer Control), whose accountability is OSWorld 2.0, BrowseComp, Zapier AutomationBench, Online-Mind2Web. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t13.error.error_recovery_agent@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **failure classification and recovery-strategy selection** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **Online-Mind2Web** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **state restoration and safe-point rollback** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **OSWorld 2.0** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **learned recovery patterns from past failures**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **BrowseComp**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **recovery success rate measurement on injected-failure scenarios** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **Zapier AutomationBench** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

<a id="p0649-agent-scaling"></a>
#### P0649 · `agent_scaling` — 1000-Agent Scale Coordination

`parts/t13_agents/P0649_agent_scaling.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t13.agent.agent_scaling@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 41000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T13.md#p0649-agent-scaling) · [full prompt](prompts/P0649_agent_scaling.txt)

**Description.** Proves the orchestration works at the target scale. This part belongs to T13 (Agents, Tool Use & Computer Control), whose accountability is OSWorld 2.0, BrowseComp, Zapier AutomationBench, Online-Mind2Web. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t13.agent.agent_scaling@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **hierarchical coordination topology for 1000 concurrent agents**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **BrowseComp** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **communication and coordination overhead measurement at scale** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Zapier AutomationBench**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **failure isolation so one agent cannot stall the swarm** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **Online-Mind2Web** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **throughput and quality measurement at 1, 10, 100, 1000 agents** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **OSWorld 2.0** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t13.agent.agent_speed@1`, `cap.t07.summarisation.summarisation_memory@1`, `cap.t10.outcome.outcome_verifier@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Safety obligation (C8, fail-closed).** This part performs or enables external effects, so every effect is routed through `cap.t19.gate.action_filter@1` at *call* time — not as a static dependency, which would make the graph cyclic. If the gate is absent the part must refuse the effect and emit OmegaCode 6001.

<a id="p0651-image-encoder"></a>
#### P0651 · `image_encoder` — High-Resolution Image Encoder

`parts/t14_perception/P0651_image_encoder.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t14.image.image_encoder@1` · determinism `seeded` · p99 ≤ 43000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T14.md#p0651-image-encoder) · [full prompt](prompts/P0651_image_encoder.txt)

**Description.** Sees fine detail in large images without losing the whole picture. This part belongs to T14 (Multimodal Perception & Grounding), whose accountability is MMMU, OSWorld 2.0. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t14.image.image_encoder@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **native-resolution tiled encoding with global-context tokens** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **OSWorld 2.0** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **adaptive token allocation by region information density** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **MMMU** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **aspect-ratio preservation without distortion artifacts**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **OSWorld 2.0**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **detail-recovery measurement on small-text and fine-structure probes** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **MMMU** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 5 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t05.causal.causal_model@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t14_perception/P0697_perception_eval_harness.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t14.perception.perception_eval_harness@1` · determinism `seeded` · p99 ≤ 42000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T14.md#p0697-perception-eval-harness) · [full prompt](prompts/P0697_perception_eval_harness.txt)

**Description.** Measures perception on every major public benchmark. This part belongs to T14 (Multimodal Perception & Grounding), whose accountability is MMMU, OSWorld 2.0. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t14.perception.perception_eval_harness@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **MMMU, document, chart, video and audio benchmark harnesses**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **OSWorld 2.0** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **MMMU**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **comparison methodology versus Opus 5's reported multimodal scores** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Its contribution is measured against **OSWorld 2.0** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **target: MMMU 99.0% versus Opus 5's ~93%** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **MMMU** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

#### P0701 · `artifact_model` — Artifact Data Model & Lifecycle

`parts/t15_generation/P0701_artifact_model.ts` · TypeScript 5.7 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t15.artifact.artifact_model@1` · determinism `seeded` · p99 ≤ 46000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T15.md#p0701-artifact-model) · [full prompt](prompts/P0701_artifact_model.txt)

**Description.** Every output is a versioned, addressable, revisable object. This part belongs to T15 (Generation, Artifacts & Interface Craft), whose accountability is GDPval-AA v2 (Elo), MMMU. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t15.artifact.artifact_model@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **artifact schema with type, version, provenance and revision history**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **MMMU**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **immutable versions with diff-based revision chains** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **dependency tracking between artifacts** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **MMMU** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **lifecycle state machine with validation at every transition** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t10.numeric.numeric_reasoning@1`, `cap.t14.modality.modality_translation@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Safety obligation (C8, fail-closed).** This part performs or enables external effects, so every effect is routed through `cap.t19.gate.action_filter@1` at *call* time — not as a static dependency, which would make the graph cyclic. If the gate is absent the part must refuse the effect and emit OmegaCode 6001.

<a id="p0751-domain-pack-framework"></a>
#### P0751 · `domain_pack_framework` — Domain Pack Framework & Interface

`parts/t16_domains/P0751_domain_pack_framework.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t16.domain.domain_pack_framework@1` · determinism `pure` · p99 ≤ 49000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T16.md#p0751-domain-pack-framework) · [full prompt](prompts/P0751_domain_pack_framework.txt)

**Description.** The uniform structure every domain expertise module follows. This part belongs to T16 (Domain Superintelligence Packs), whose accountability is GPQA Diamond, Life-sciences suite, GDPval-AA v2 (Elo). It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t16.domain.domain_pack_framework@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **domain pack schema: ontology, verifiers, tools, benchmarks, guardrails** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Life-sciences suite** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
2. Implement **capability registration and routing by detected domain** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
3. Implement **domain-confidence estimation and cross-domain handoff**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **GPQA Diamond** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
4. Implement **pack conformance test suite all 40 domain packs must pass** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Life-sciences suite** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t10.numeric.numeric_reasoning@1`, `cap.t11.spec.spec_language@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

#### P0801 · `data_sourcing` — Training Data Sourcing & Licensing

`parts/t17_training/P0801_data_sourcing.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t17.data.data_sourcing@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 5000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T17.md#p0801-data-sourcing) · [full prompt](prompts/P0801_data_sourcing.txt)

**Description.** Legally clean, high-quality data at petabyte scale. This part belongs to T17 (Training, Data & Recursive Self-Improvement), whose accountability is Frontier-Bench v0.1, ARC-AGI-3. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t17.data.data_sourcing@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **source inventory with license classification and permission tracking**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **ARC-AGI-3** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **acquisition pipeline with robots/terms compliance verification** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Frontier-Bench v0.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **provenance recording at document granularity** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **ARC-AGI-3**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **auditable license-compliance report for the whole corpus** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **Frontier-Bench v0.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

It requires 7 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t05.causal.causal_model@1`, `cap.t06.conditional.conditional_layers@1`, `cap.t10.numeric.numeric_reasoning@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

**Description.** Trains the Ω-tokeniser that fixes the token tax. This part belongs to T17 (Training, Data & Recursive Self-Improvement), whose accountability is Frontier-Bench v0.1, ARC-AGI-3. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t17.tokenizer.tokenizer_training@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **vocabulary learning with multilingual and code fairness objectives** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **Frontier-Bench v0.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **compression-rate measurement per language and domain** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **ARC-AGI-3** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **boundary-quality evaluation for math, code and rare scripts** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **Frontier-Bench v0.1**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

Implement **target: significantly fewer tokens per text than the Opus 4.7+ tokenizer**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **ARC-AGI-3** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

#### P0849 · `training_bench` — Training Infrastructure Benchmark Suite

`parts/t17_training/P0849_training_bench.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t17.training.training_bench@1` · determinism `io` · p99 ≤ 6000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T17.md#p0849-training-bench) · [full prompt](prompts/P0849_training_bench.txt)

**Description.** Measures the training system itself. This part belongs to T17 (Training, Data & Recursive Self-Improvement), whose accountability is Frontier-Bench v0.1, ARC-AGI-3. It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t17.training.training_bench@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **throughput, utilisation and scaling-efficiency benchmarks**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Its contribution is measured against **ARC-AGI-3** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
2. Implement **stability and recovery benchmarks under injected faults** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **Frontier-Bench v0.1** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
3. Implement **comparison against published large-scale training efficiency** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **ARC-AGI-3**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
4. Implement **regression gates for infrastructure changes** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **Frontier-Bench v0.1** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.

<a id="p0851-eval-framework"></a>
#### P0851 · `eval_framework` — Evaluation Framework Core

`parts/t18_eval/P0851_eval_framework.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t18.eval.eval_framework@1` · determinism `seeded` · p99 ≤ 8000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T18.md#p0851-eval-framework) · [full prompt](prompts/P0851_eval_framework.txt)

**Description.** The uniform harness every benchmark plugs into. This part belongs to T18 (Evaluation, Benchmarking & Dominance Proofs), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified, ARC-AGI-3, OSWorld 2.0, GDPval-AA v2 (Elo). It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t18.eval.eval_framework@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **task/harness/grader abstraction with strict isolation between them** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **deterministic execution with full result provenance** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. Its contribution is measured against **SWE-bench Verified** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **parallel evaluation across 1000 workers with reproducible aggregation**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **ARC-AGI-3** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **framework conformance suite for all harness implementations** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **OSWorld 2.0**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 6 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t01.string.string_interning@1`, `cap.t12.flaky.flaky_detection@1`, `cap.t13.agent.agent_communication@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.

`parts/t18_eval/P0893_eval_reproducibility.py` · Python 3.13 · **5000 lines** · publishes `cap.t18.eval.eval_reproducibility@1` · determinism `seeded` · p99 ≤ 3000 ns · [full spec](docs/PART_SPECS_T18.md#p0893-eval-reproducibility) · [full prompt](prompts/P0893_eval_reproducibility.txt)

**Description.** Anyone can verify every number we publish. This part belongs to T18 (Evaluation, Benchmarking & Dominance Proofs), whose accountability is SWE-bench Verified, ARC-AGI-3, OSWorld 2.0, GDPval-AA v2 (Elo). It is built by a single isolated worker and links to the rest of the system only through the Ω-Bus capability `cap.t18.eval.eval_reproducibility@1`; it imports no sibling part. Its four mandated mechanisms are:

1. Implement **complete reproduction package: code, configs, task hashes, environments**, and make it correct under concurrency: at least 64 in-flight `OmegaEnvelope`s must be able to traverse it simultaneously. No lock, mutex or borrow may be held across an `await` / `.await` / `yield` boundary, and the part must expose a contention counter so T09 can attribute latency to it. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **ARC-AGI-3**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.
2. Implement **independent-reproduction verification protocol** with an explicit *a-priori* cost model. Before doing the work the part must be able to state the tokens, FLOPs and microseconds it intends to consume, and it must abort with an `OmegaError` in the 4xxx budget range rather than silently exceed the envelope's `budget` or `deadline_ns`. Its contribution is measured against **OSWorld 2.0** — a regression on that benchmark is an automatic rejection of this part.
3. Implement **raw-result publication with per-item outcomes** together with its verification path, so that anything this mechanism produces can be independently re-checked *inside this same file* without contacting any other part. The checker must be cheap enough to run on every call in debug mode and must be wired into `selftest()`. Correctness here is what makes the tier's **GDPval-AA v2 (Elo)** target reachable; the part therefore ships a microbenchmark that stands in for that benchmark's inner loop.
4. Implement **reproduction-success verification by external parties** as a first-class, fully realised mechanism. No stub, no `NotImplementedError`, no configuration flag whose default disables it. Its state must be reportable through `describe()` and it must be exercised by at least eight in-file tests, including one that fails loudly if the mechanism is silently bypassed. This mechanism sits on the critical path of **SWE-bench Verified**, so its p99 latency assertion is part of the acceptance criteria, not an optional extra.

It requires 7 capabilities — `cap.t01.abi.abi_types@1`, `cap.t01.abi.abi_errors@1`, `cap.t01.omega.omega_bus_core@1`, `cap.t18.dynamic.dynamic_benchmark@1`, `cap.t01.task.task_runtime@1`, `cap.t12.migration.migration_engine@1`, `cap.t13.business.business_automation@1` — and must ship a working local fallback for each, so that the file remains usable when the other 999 workers' output is absent.
